title: Talking about the future
description: Say what you will do and what will happen with ska, kommer att, tänker and the present.

guide.summary: Swedish has no future ending. You say what will happen with ska for plans, kommer att for predictions, tänker for intentions, or simply the present with a time word. Learn which one fits and where inte and the subject go.

sections.title: Ska + infinitive: plans and decisions
sections.text: Ska is the everyday way to talk about something you have planned or decided. It never changes with the subject, and the infinitive follows it directly, just as after kan or vill.
steps: Ask: has someone planned or decided this?
If yes, write ska, the same for every subject.
Add the infinitive, the dictionary form ending in -a, with no att.

examples.en: I am going to travel to Gothenburg.

examples.sv: Vi ska köpa en ny bil.
examples.en: We are going to buy a new car.

watch: Never ska att: ska works like kan and vill.
Skall is the old written form; write ska.

sections.title: Kommer att + infinitive: predictions
sections.text: Kommer att predicts what will happen when nobody decides it: the weather, results, feelings. Kommer does not change with the subject, att follows, then the infinitive.
steps: Ask: is this a prediction rather than a plan?
Write kommer, then att.
Finish with the infinitive.

examples.sv: Det kommer att regna i helgen.

watch: Kommer takes att, ska does not.
In speech people often drop att: det kommer regna. Write it with att.
Ska with weather sounds like a plan or a report: det ska regna means it is supposed to rain.

sections.title: The present + a time word
sections.text: When a time word already says when, Swedish often uses the plain present for the future, especially for timetables and arrangements.

rows: She is coming home on Friday.

steps: Check the sentence has a time word in the future.
Keep the verb in the ordinary present, ending in -r.

examples.en: We are going to Malmö tomorrow.

watch: Imorgon and ikväll are also written i morgon and i kväll; both are correct.
Without a time word, the present usually means now.

sections.title: Tänker + infinitive: intentions
sections.text: Tänker is the present of tänka, think. Followed directly by an infinitive, it means intend to: a personal intention, a little stronger than ska.
steps: Check the speaker intends to do something.
Write tänker, the same for every subject.
Add the infinitive with no att.

examples.sv: Jag tänker köpa en ny cykel.
examples.en: I intend to buy a new bike.
She intends to move to Stockholm.

watch: No att: tänker sluta, not tänker att sluta.
Tänker på means think about, not intend.

sections.title: Saying what will not happen
sections.text: Inte comes right after the first verb of the sentence: ska inte, kommer inte att, tänker inte.

rows: I am not going to work.
She does not intend to stop.

steps: Find the finite verb: ska, kommer, tänker or the present verb.
Put inte right after it.
With kommer, att follows inte.

examples.en: He is not going to drive.

examples.sv: Det kommer inte att bli varmt.

watch: Never inte before the finite verb in a main clause.
Kommer inte att, not kommer att inte.

sections.title: A time word first: the verb stays second
sections.text: Swedish keeps the finite verb in second place. If a time word starts the sentence, the subject moves after the verb.
steps: See what stands first: subject or time word.
Put the finite verb in second place.
If the time word is first, the subject comes right after the verb.
The infinitive comes after the subject.

examples.en: Tomorrow I am going to clean.

examples.sv: I helgen ska jag hälsa på mormor.
examples.en: This weekend I am going to visit Grandma.

watch: Never Imorgon jag ska: English word order breaks the verb-second rule.
A long time phrase like nästa vecka still counts as one first element.

steps: Ask whether it is a plan or a decision.
Write ska, unchanged for every subject.
Add the infinitive directly, no att.
Ask whether it is a prediction nobody controls.
Write kommer att.
Add the infinitive.
Find the time word that points to the future.
Use the ordinary present, ending in -r.
Check it is an intention.
Write tänker, then the infinitive with no att.
Find the finite verb.
Put inte right after it.
With kommer, att comes after inte.
See whether a time word comes first.
Keep the finite verb second.
Put the subject right after the verb, then the infinitive.
